findings.message: `string.match(...)` runs before the validity check. If the input is not a string (undefined, null, a number or an object), it throws a TypeError instead of returning false. Every other `isValid*` helper in this file returns false for bad input: `isValidCIDR` catches the error, and `isValidFourPartDecimal` only calls `.match` after `isValid` has passed. Callers that rely on this boolean to validate untrusted input can crash. Call `isValidCIDR` first (it already returns false for non-strings) and only run the regex after it passes, or add a type check.

The prefix part isn't held to the same strict format as the address part. Because `\d+` accepts leading zeros, strings like `1.2.3.4/032` or `1.2.3.4/0008` pass. A function meant to enforce strict decimal notation would be expected to reject them, since leading zeros are rejected in the octets. The regex also repeats the one in `parseCIDR`, so the two have to be kept in sync by hand. Consider `/^(.+)\/(0|[1-9]\d?)$/`, or reuse the parse result.

This adds a new public API with no tests in `test/ipaddr.test.js` and no README entry, while the neighbouring `isValidFourPartDecimal` has both. Edge cases such as `10.1/8`, `1.2.3.4/33`, `0x01.2.3.4/8`, leading-zero prefixes and non-string input are not covered. The committed `ipaddr.min.js` is also not regenerated, so the minified build has no such function.
